notes: Compiled from 6 independent persona rounds. Hallway tests still required before live.

scenarios.text: I logged food for 4 days then ghosted the app until Sunday.
I have MyFitnessPal, Hevy, and a water app, and none of them know I skipped the gym all week.
My streak died on day 6 so I deleted the widget so I wouldn't see the goose egg.
I installed a 25-minute study timer for the cert, used it twice, and now it's just a red badge I ignore.
It's 6:15 and I'm standing in the fridge deciding between takeout and the same chicken again.
I bought spinach on Sunday and found it slime in the crisper on Thursday.
I meal-prepped Sunday, ate it Monday, and ordered DoorDash the rest of the week.
I skip lunch between classes, graze on cereal, then Uber Eats at 9 because nothing is actually planned.
I said I'd be in bed at 10 and I'm still scrolling at 12:40.
I sleep at 1am on weeknights, then 'catch up' Saturday until noon and feel worse.
I set a wind-down alarm, snoozed it, and opened one more YouTube video.
I study until 1am because that's the only quiet hour, then I'm wrecked for the 8am shift.
I remember the refill when the bottle has two pills left and the pharmacy is already closed.
I rescheduled the dentist twice and the reminder card is still on the fridge from March.
I take the morning med with coffee on weekdays and completely blank on weekends.
The physical was supposed to happen before my insurance year reset and I missed it.
I have 47 Udemy courses at 12% and I keep buying the next one when it's $11.99.
My Coursera tab has said Resume for eight months and I still pay the monthly.
I paid for a bootcamp cohort, missed week 3, and never logged back in.
I bought a 12-week lifting program in January and I'm still on week 2 in September.
My AWS cert expires in six weeks and I haven't sat a practice exam.
I passed the exam last year and I couldn't answer the same question if you asked me tonight.
HR asked for the PDF of my cert and I spent 40 minutes digging through old email.
I told people I was 'working on the PMP' in January and it's September.
I took great Notion notes in the course and I can't find the one trick I need tonight.
My highlight export from three books is a 90-page dump I never reopen.
I wrote Anki cards for two weeks, then the deck sat untouched until the night before the exam.
I recorded the lecture on my phone and never replayed it because I don't remember which file it is.
I watch the tutorial at 1.5x, nod along, then never open the editor.
I blocked Saturday morning for LeetCode and cleaned the kitchen instead.
I can explain the concept out loud and then freeze when I have to do it without the video.
I saved 40 workout videos to Watch later and I've actually done two of them.
I open an EOB and still can't tell if we owe $40 or $400.
A hospital bill shows up three months later for a visit I thought insurance already closed.
I pay Mom's copay at the desk and then get another bill at home for the same visit.
The kids' urgent-care bills sit in a drawer because I don't know which ones are actually paid.
A streaming charge hits the joint card that neither of us remembers turning on.
The kids' school and game apps auto-renew and I only notice on the statement.
Mom's pharmacy auto-ship keeps charging after we already switched her meds.
I cancel a subscription and it still bills us the next month.
My spouse 'handles the bills' until a late notice shows up and they didn't.
We both think the other one paid the electric bill until it's past due.
I put the sitter on my card and then forget to pull it from the joint account.
Our 529 contribution skips a month and nobody notices until the quarterly email.
I pay at least one late fee most months.
The HOA and property-tax envelopes sit unopened until a penalty letter arrives.
Tax season starts and I'm still hunting W-2s, 1099s, and the daycare receipt.
I can't add up Mom's medical expenses because the receipts are in three different places.
A permission slip lives in a backpack until the morning it's due.
I fill out the same emergency-contact form for school, camp, and soccer every season.
The IEP packet sits on the counter because I don't know which pages need a signature.
Sports physicals and shot records are in three portals and I still can't print one by Friday.
Mom's Medicare mail comes to our house and I don't know what actually needs an answer.
A doctor's office asks for Mom's power of attorney and I still can't put my hands on it.
The pharmacy wants a prior-auth form that's in her purse or our junk drawer.
I leave her specialist visit with no notes and then can't remember what they changed.
The kitchen counter is a stack of mail I swear I'll sort this weekend.
I photograph a form with my phone and then can't find it when school asks again.
Appliance warranties and HOA PDFs live in two inboxes and a drawer.
I recycle a letter that turns out to be something we needed to keep.
A school conference is on my spouse's calendar and I find out the morning of.
Two kids' practices and Mom's appointment land on the same afternoon and nobody flags it.
I say yes to a birthday party and then forget to tell anyone else in the house.
The pediatrician reminder is a sticky note that fell off the fridge.
I accept a meeting invite and only notice it overlaps something I already had once I'm already late.
I keep a work calendar and a phone calendar, and they never agree on where I'm supposed to be.
My partner books dinner on a night I already have a work thing, and we find out that afternoon.
I spend Sunday night dragging calendar blocks around just to make next week physically possible.
I sit through 30-minute meetings that could have been a three-line email.
I leave a call with no notes and later text someone, wait, what did we decide?
Recurring meetings stay on my calendar long after nobody has anything to say.
I get invited to a meeting with no agenda and still feel rude declining it.
I block focus time on my calendar and people still drop meetings on top of it.
I don't start real work until after 4 because the day filled with quick calls.
I eat lunch at my desk on a call I didn't need to be on.
I decline a meeting and then get pinged asking why I wasn't there.
I miss school pickup because a work meeting ran long and nobody flagged the conflict.
Doctor and dentist appointments live in my head until the reminder text the morning of.
Work travel shows up on the family calendar two days before I leave.
I get pulled into a parent conference during my only prep period because nobody checked the duty roster.
I open email, answer two things, and somehow have more unread than when I started.
Important mail sits under newsletters I keep meaning to unsubscribe from.
I search my inbox for something I know I saw last week and still can't find it.
I archive a thread so I can deal with it later, and then it vanishes from my brain.
I star a message so I'll reply later, and later never comes.
I type a reply, get interrupted, and the draft sits there for days.
I tell someone I'll get back to you this afternoon, and then I don't.
I see a text from my supervisor during a shift, say I'll answer on break, and forget until I'm already home.
I owe someone an answer and only remember when they ping me again.
I wait on a reply, forget I was waiting, and the thing just dies.
I promised to send a file after a call and find the reminder three days later in my notes app.
I follow up once, feel annoying, and then never follow up again.
Family texts, work Slack, and email all buzz at once and I answer the wrong one first.
I miss a can-you-pick-up-milk text because Slack ate the notification.
I check three chat apps every morning just to be sure I didn't miss my boss.
A group chat with 40 unread messages sits on top of the one message that actually needed me.
I last posted in February. I only remember when a customer asks if we're still in business.
Sunday night I open Instagram, stare at a blank box, and close it so I can pack the truck.
The crew finished three bathrooms this week and the page still shows last summer's deck.
I told myself I'd post every job. I post when I feel guilty, which is never on a busy week.
I mean to ask for a Google review when we wrap a job, then the truck is already rolling.
We have 11 Google reviews from 2022 and the kitchen is busier than it's ever been.
Customers text me 'you guys were great' and I never turn that into a public review.
I only remember to ask when they're already walking out the warehouse door with the invoice.
Before-and-after shots of the tile job are still in my camera roll from March.
The line cook sent me tonight's special. It's sitting in a group chat I haven't opened.
I have 400 job photos on my phone and zero of them made it to the page.
The warehouse restock looked great. That picture is buried under 80 screenshots of tracking numbers.
Every post I start with 'Another happy customer!' and delete it because it sounds fake.
I rewrite the HVAC tune-up caption from scratch because I can never find last month's.
I don't know what to say about a pick-pack warehouse job so I just don't post.
I asked ChatGPT once, hated the voice, and went back to posting nothing.
I still personally read every Indeed application at 10pm after the warehouse closes.
Forty applicants for dishwasher. I hired the one who texted me back first.
The Indeed inbox is a graveyard. I last opened it when we were already short two techs.
My hiring process is screenshotting résumés and texting whoever looks like they can drive a van.
New hires fill out a paper packet I printed in 2019 and nobody knows where the W-4s go.
Day one is a manila folder, a faded handbook, and 'follow Mike on the truck.'
The line cook's first day was a photocopy of the allergy sheet and a locker combo on a sticky note.
I still collect I-9s in an office drawer that only I have a key to.
Tomorrow's shift lives in a group text with 40 unread messages and three people who already quit.
I text the whole HVAC crew about Saturday and get six thumbs-up and two 'what?'
Kitchen call-outs happen in a thread named TEAM!!! with old vendors still in it.
The warehouse lead texts me, I text the picker, the picker texts the driver. Nobody has the same list.
Someone no-shows the breakfast shift and I find out when the tickets start stacking.
I find out a tech isn't coming when the customer calls asking where we are.
Call-outs land as 'can't come' at 4:45am with no list of who else is free.
We lost two warehouse pickers this month and I still don't have a standby list.
Tomorrow's board has two techs on the same 10am and nobody noticed until the customer called from the driveway.
I rebuild the day's route in a spreadsheet every morning because Jobber/Housecall Pro lists jobs in the order they were booked, not the order that makes sense on the map.
A tech is sitting in a parking lot texting 'what's next?' while the next job is 40 minutes the other way.
We promised a 2-hour window and the van is still at the supply house because dispatch never checked that the part was actually on the truck.
Shopify says 14 in stock, the warehouse bin has 3, and we just sold 8 on a flash sale.
The SKU on the packing slip doesn't match the SKU in the spreadsheet, so pickers guess and we ship the wrong variant.
Housecall Pro says the part is 'on the truck' and the tech is at Home Depot buying it again.
Reorder points live in my head. We stock out of the one SKU that actually sells and the rest of the shelf is dead weight.
Returns sit in a pile by the back door until I steal a Sunday to decide restock vs refund vs trash.
The customer already got the Shopify refund and the 3PL still shows the unit inbound, so inventory double-counts until I untangle it by hand.
Every wrong-address / split-shipment / backorder exception becomes a 20-minute email thread, and I am the middle of it.
I reprint packing slips by hand because the 3PL portal and Shopify disagree on what actually shipped.
Every night I copy completed jobs out of Jobber/Housecall Pro into QuickBooks, then into a spreadsheet so the owner can see the day.
The same customer has three names — one in Jobber, one in QuickBooks, one in the sheet. I am the merge algorithm.
The job is marked done in the field app and still not an invoice, because I haven't done the 11pm paste yet.
I keep a running Google Sheet of 'what the software got wrong today' because nobody trusts any one system.
I send an invoice and then forget to chase it for 3 weeks.
The job was finished Friday; the invoice is still a draft because I have to retype line items from Jobber into QuickBooks.
Net-30 customers pay on day 62 and my only reminder system is scrolling the aging report when cash feels tight.
Stripe/Square deposits hit the bank and I match them to invoices by eyeballing amounts.
Month-end is a weekend of uncategorized QuickBooks transactions and a folder of 'ask the owner' screenshots.
The bank feed is 200 uncleared lines because Shopify payouts, refunds, and fees all land as mystery deposits.
The P&L is a lie until I fix inventory COGS by hand, so we never actually close.
The accountant asks for 'the usual packet' and I spend two nights exporting CSVs that still don't match.
Techs text their hours from the field; I retype them into Gusto and pray the overtime math is right.
January is 1099 panic: 40 contractors, half the W-9s missing, and last year's sheet has three spellings of the same person.
A new 1099 vendor got paid from three different cards plus Venmo and none of it is tagged contractor.
Payroll is 'done' when I click submit, then I spend an hour pasting the register into QuickBooks so the books aren't a lie.
Receipts live in a camera roll, a glovebox, and my inbox. April is a shoebox.
Sales tax in Shopify, the 3PL, and QuickBooks are three different numbers and I pick one for the return.
I cannot tell you what we owe in quarterly estimates without opening six tabs.
Mileage, job materials, and Amazon business orders never make it into the write-off pile until tax week.
A Facebook lead sat 6 hours because I was on a job.
A Zillow lead hits during a showing and I don't reply until I'm in the car at 9.
Someone calls about a rental while I'm at a handover and the voicemail is still unplayed.
I silence a Google lead ping to finish the install and they already booked the other guy.
The couple who loved the house Saturday went quiet because I never sent the 'just checking in' text.
I quoted a condenser last Tuesday and never followed up, and now they're not answering.
A guest asked about next month, I starred the Turo thread, and I still haven't answered.
Open-house sign-ins from two weeks ago are still on a clipboard in the truck.
I scribble a price on a notepad in the driveway and then can't read it when I get home.
They asked for a written quote on Monday and I'm still building it in my head.
I texted a round number, they wanted it on letterhead, and I never sent the PDF.
Every rental quote means I open the calendar, a spreadsheet, and three old DMs.
The same buyer DMed me on Instagram, emailed, and texted, and I answered two of the three.
Facebook, the business cell, and Housecall Pro all have the same AC lead and I don't know which thread is current.
A guest is in Turo chat, SMS, and email and I keep repeating myself.
I copy names from Zillow into my notes app and still lose who wanted the Tuesday showing.
The no-cool call came in at 11pm and I found the voicemail at 7am — they already hired the 24-hour shop.
Saturday the van number filled up with lockout calls and I didn't hear them until Monday.
A buyer texted 'can we see it tonight' at 8:30 and I was at my kid's game with the ringer off.
The lockbox-code question hit Turo at 1am and I was asleep, so they left a one-star.
The homeowner texts 'where is the tech' four times before I can pull over.
I promised a callback when the part came in and they had to chase me two days later.
The renter asks for the gate code again because I sent it in the wrong thread.
A client texts 'did the other side sign?' during a showing and I don't see it until I'm back in the car.
I finished a 5-star job last week and never texted the Google review link.
The only reviews that show up are the mad ones, because happy people don't think to post.
I screenshot the review link after every walkthrough and still forget to send it.
The closing went great and I never asked them to review me on Google or Zillow.
An angry Facebook comment sat for two days because I don't check the Page inbox.
They replied on my Google listing instead of calling, and I only saw it after the one-star.
A guest's damage dispute sat in email while I was answering Turo chat.
The inspection objection landed in the brokerage portal and I was only watching my phone texts.
